extracted.intended_audience: rulers/princes and their advisors; readers of political-military counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and historical examples about how a prince should secure, maintain, and extend power — covering military preparation, deception, lawmaking, use of fortune, and decisively handling rivals. Drawn from narrative examples (Duke Valentino, Castruccio Castracani).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify war as necessary and invoke divine favour
rubrics_metrics.description: War is just when it is necessary; 'arms are hallowed when there is no other hope but in them.' Divine signs and providence that have favoured you should be cited as justification and encouragement to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text points to miracles and providential signs (sea divided, manna, rock giving water) as tokens that God has assisted and that the prince ought to complete what Fortune has begun; 'God is not willing to do everything' — the prince must act to win glory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish new laws and ordinances when newly risen
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing honours a man more than to establish new laws and new ordinances when he himself was newly risen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-founded and dignified new laws will make a new ruler revered and admired; Italy contains opportunities to introduce such innovations in every form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have your own reliable forces
rubrics_metrics.description: As a true foundation for every enterprise, be provided with your own forces, because there can be no more faithful, truer, or better soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though individual soldiers may be good, they are far better when commanded by their prince, honoured by him, and maintained at his expense. Prepare such arms to defend against foreigners by native valour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer native/own troops to mercenaries and foreign forces
rubrics_metrics.description: A prince should rely on his own forces rather than mercenaries or foreign troops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Native troops are more faithful; the narrative contrasts Italian shortcomings in leadership with the fidelity of troops maintained and commanded by their prince.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit enemy weaknesses and innovate military organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the defects of enemy infantries (e.g., Spaniards and Switzers) and invent a variation on existing arms to combine their strengths/avoid their weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Spaniards cannot resist cavalry; Switzers fear infantry; invent a third order that resists cavalry and is not afraid of infantry. Such improvements confer reputation and power on a new prince.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize political opportunity to present yourself as liberator
rubrics_metrics.description: When the country suffers under foreign dominion, the prince who takes up the charge of liberating it will be received with love and obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The populace's thirst for revenge, devotion, and tears will open doors and remove envy; the prince should act with courage and hope to ennoble his native country under his standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use temporizing, negotiation, and deception to buy time
rubrics_metrics.description: While negotiating reconciliation and appearing conciliatory, secretly prepare forces and plans to neutralize opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duke Valentino temporized with reconciliations while enlisting men-at-arms and dispersing troops covertly; reconciliation served as cover for gathering strength and arranging traps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrupt opponents with gifts and promises to divide them
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrupt or corruptible figures among opponents can be bribed or promised preferment to secure their cooperation or neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duke corrupted Pagolo Orsini with gifts and promises, which helped persuade stubborn opponents to wait and lowered their guard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use invitations and private meetings as means to seize rivals
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange that opponents come to you unarmed or in situations where their guards are away, then detain them and have them seized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valentino invited leaders to meet, placed them between men commissioned to look after them, and had them taken into a secret chamber and made prisoners when circumstances allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutralize or eliminate conspirators decisively
rubrics_metrics.description: Once seized or when necessary to secure the state, remove traitors or dangerous rivals without hesitation (e.g., by strangling or execution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duke caused Vitellozzo, Oliverotto, Pagolo and Duke di Gravina to be strangled after ensuring the pope's actions; decisive killings prevented future dangers. The duke also killed some of his own soldiers to stop a sack—using decisive violence to maintain control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress excesses among your troops to preserve order
rubrics_metrics.description: When soldiers commit outrages (sacking, pillage), the prince must repress them decisively to prevent further disorder or reputation damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Sinigalia was sacked, the duke killed some of his soldiers to stop the outrage and restore order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feign weakness or fear to encourage enemy overconfidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Appear fearful or weak to induce the enemy to be overconfident and expose tactical vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio showed signs of fear and did not use his munitions, encouraging the enemy's insolence; when they were emboldened he struck using prepared tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Array troops tactically: strong flanks, weaker center
rubrics_metrics.description: Place your most valiant men on the wings and the less reliable in the center, so that when battle occurs the strong wings can rout the enemy while the center remains disengaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio reversed the enemy's deployment (enemy strongest in center) and used rapid wing movements while holding the center back, producing a rout and heavy enemy losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tactical maneuver (slow center, rapid wings) to isolate enemy parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Command center squadrons to march slowly while moving the wings rapidly forward so only the wings engage and the center of the enemy cannot assist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This maneuver allowed Castruccio to oppose his best soldiers to the weaker parts of the enemy and prevented coordination, leading to complete defeat of the foe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gain popular support and exploit civic institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Win the people's affection and use public pressure or civic institutions to secure freedom, rank, or authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio's release after popular tumult led to his election as captain and later creation as lord of Lucca; popular unrest and demands can be leveraged to political advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate alliances with powerful external figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Make friends with external potentates or emperors to gain titles, privileges, and legitimacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio met Frederick of Bavaria, received privileges and appointment as the emperor's lieutenant, and was created lord of Pisa—using external legitimacy to strengthen domestic position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exiles and external forces to recover or enlarge power
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep contact with exiles sympathetic to your cause and coordinate with external lords to regain territory or influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio worked with exiled Ghibellines and Uguccione to mount returns and sieges that expanded his control in Lunigiana and other regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare fortifications and logistical supplies for sieges
rubrics_metrics.description: Fortify strong points, stock supplies and munitions so they can withstand sieges and serve as bases for operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio fortified the tower of the Onesti, provisioned it to stand a siege, constructed forts (e.g., Zerezzanello) and used these to capture towns and besiege strategic passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit timing and fortune; seize political openings
rubrics_metrics.description: Fortune often gives openings (internal disorder, foreign distractions) that a shrewd prince should seize promptly to advance his position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Castruccio capitalized on Pisan rebellion against Uguccione and the people's tumult to free him; Machiavelli emphasizes lowly or adverse beginnings and the role of Fortune in enabling great deeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate personal virtues and modest demeanour to gain trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Display modesty, courtesy, and deference to gain love and trust among different social ranks, making it easier to gather followers and power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Castruccio's modesty, courtesy, and accomplishments made him beloved, helped secure appointments, and allowed him to convert popularity into formal authority.
